description: End of file on XREFFILE and the CLOSE that follows it - the four CALLs that end CBSTM03A's statement loop, pinned as one sequence. Where this sits in the caller. 1000-MAINLINE at app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:316-329 is PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' wrapped around 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT (:319); the loop is left only when a READ reports '10' and :357 moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE, and the next thing the program does after :329 is PERFORM 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE (:333). This case is that ending, transcribed: an OPEN, a READ that succeeds, a READ that reaches end of file, and the CLOSE. case05 pins the OPEN alone, case06 the first READ alone and case07 a three-row browse that never reaches the end; what is unique here is the boundary itself and what survives across it. Dispatch. EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD at app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:118 selects WHEN 'XREFFILE' at :121 and performs 2000-XREFFILE-PROC THRU 2999-EXIT at :122 - the SECOND of the four arms, so all four calls below prove the ordered EVALUATE reaches it rather than stopping at 'TRNXFILE' (:119), and LK-M03B-DD is pinned on every one of them so the arm cannot be reached by accident (gate G30). The guarded paragraph, and the guard that does not fire. 2000-XREFFILE-PROC (:157-179) is three independent guards, each leaving the paragraph the moment it fires. On both READs, IF M03B-OPEN at :159 is FALSE and control falls through to IF M03B-READ at :164, which does READ XREF-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT at :165-166 and then GO TO 2900-EXIT at :167 - so :170's IF M03B-CLOSE is never even evaluated on a read. On the CLOSE, :159 and :164 are both false and :170 fires, doing CLOSE XREF-FILE at :171 then GO TO 2900-EXIT at :172. All three paths converge on 2900-EXIT (:175-176), whose single statement is MOVE XREFFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC, and then on 2999-EXIT (:178-179). The guard order is behaviour rather than style (gate G30, rule R7). One status area, read twice, two different answers. Every LK-M03B-RC below is that one MOVE at :176 reading the XREFFILE-STATUS area declared at :87-89 - two bytes of its own, distinct from TRNXFILE-STATUS at :83-85, CUSTFILE-STATUS at :91-93 and ACCTFILE-STATUS at :95-97 (gate G47). That is what makes the '10' and the '00' after it worth pinning together: the third call leaves XREFFILE-STATUS at '10' on AT END, and the fourth must report '00' out of that same area once the CLOSE has set it. A '10' still visible in the CLOSE image would mean :176 had moved a stale or a shared status rather than this file's own, and no other case in the folder would catch it. None of the four areas carries a VALUE clause, so a status is only ever what the last operation on THAT file put there (practice B7) - which is why the sequence opens the file first rather than reading an inherited status. What survives the end of file, and why the area is deliberately not cleared first. READ ... INTO at :165 is the only statement in the paragraph that touches LK-M03B-FLDT, and on AT END it moves nothing at all - so the record area comes back exactly as the caller left it. Asserting that requires the caller NOT to have blanked it: 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT does issue MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT at :350 before each of its calls, but a cleared area and an unchanged area are indistinguishable, so the second READ and the CLOSE here are driven with the area left as the previous call returned it. Images 2 and 3 therefore still carry row 0 in LK-M03B-FLDT rather than spaces, and reproducing that residue is the point of pinning them. It is not a theoretical concern: :364 moves WS-M03B-FLDT into CARD-XREF-RECORD unconditionally, after the EVALUATE, so the caller copies those stale bytes on the end-of-file pass too and relies on END-OF-FILE to ignore them. The OPEN and the CLOSE are accepted by the caller at :771 and :879 on '00' OR '04', so '00' is one of two continuing values there, while the READ continues only on '00' (:354-355), takes end of file on '10' (:356-357) and abends on anything else (:358-361). Order, and the absence of a key. SELECT XREF-FILE declares ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL over RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-CARD-NUM (:37-41). Sequential access means the RECORD KEY is not consulted by a plain 'R' at all, so LK-M03B-KEY stays twenty-five spaces and LK-M03B-KEY-LN stays the zoned image of zero, '000{' - that trailing brace being a positive-sign overpunch in the low-order byte of PIC S9(4) and not a stray character. It also means one seeded row is all it takes to reach AT END on the second read, which is exactly how this case is shaped: inputs seeds row 0 and nothing else. Widths, re-derivable by hand (practice B11). Each area image is 1040 bytes because LK-M03B-AREA (:100-112) is 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000, and all six spans are named individually below so every one of those bytes is asserted field by field and not only as one string (gate G17). READ ... INTO LK-M03B-FLDT is a PIC X MOVE of a 50-byte record into a 1000-byte receiver, left-justified and space-filled, so a successful READ image is the 50 record bytes followed by 950 spaces; because row 0's 36 shipped bytes are all digits and its 14-byte FILLER normalises to spaces, LK-M03B-FLDT reads as 36 digits followed by 964 spaces. A cross-reference row is 50 bytes because app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy is XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) + XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) + XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) + FILLER X(14), which is also the width CBSTM03B's own FD splits into FD-XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) + FD-XREF-DATA X(34) at :65-68 (gate G19). Code page, named and never inferred (practice B8). Every byte above is US-ASCII, the code page of the authoritative fixtures under app/data/ASCII; IBM037 belongs to the reference-only EBCDIC datasets under app/data/EBCDIC and is deliberately not used here. The platform default is never relied on, which matters for the one character in this file that is neither a digit nor a space: the '{' of LK-M03B-KEY-LN is 0x7B in US-ASCII and a different byte entirely under an EBCDIC reading. XREF-CUST-ID and XREF-ACCT-ID are PIC 9 fields carried as character strings with their leading zeros intact - '000000050' and '00000000050' - and never as numbers, because the comparison is on bytes. The 36-versus-50 deviation (gate G16, risk R-F). cardxref.txt ships 36 bytes per record - the card number, the customer id and the account id and nothing else - where CVACT03Y declares 50 including that trailing FILLER. This case therefore declares the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation against XREFFILE and leaves the seed at its shipped width: inputs is fixture-backed, so no row is written out here and nothing in this file can pre-pad one. The absent fourteen spaces are supplied once, at seed time, by the sole owner of that pad and before anything decodes a row; the operation is idempotent, so a row already 50 wide is returned untouched, and any width that is neither 36 nor 50 is refused outright rather than repaired. Naming FILLER explicitly in the final-state row is the field-level proof that those spaces arrived: it is precisely the span the fixture omits, so a pad applied twice, or not at all, shows up there before anywhere else (gate G21). Read-only, proved twice. All four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph in CBSTM03B writes, so the one seeded row must come back exactly as it went in - and reaching end of file changes nothing about that. It is asserted row by row in expectedFinalState and again at dataset level in expectedDatasets, where XREFFILE is pinned at one row of 50 bytes on the FINAL_STATE channel and M03BAREA at four images of 1040 bytes on the WRITES channel - a count and a width no row expectation can state on its own. Real keys, not invented ones. Row 0 is the head of the coherent statement chain the four DD blocks share: XREF-CARD-NUM 0500024453765740 is the card the TRNXFILE cases carry, XREF-CUST-ID 000000050 is the key the CUSTFILE cases read by, and XREF-ACCT-ID 00000000050 is the key the ACCTFILE cases read by. The three come off one real fixture row, which is how CBSTM03A's own chain runs at :319, :321 and :322. Return code and messages. expectedReturnCode is 0 because CBSTM03B contains no RETURN-CODE reference anywhere and simply GOBACKs at :130-131; LK-M03B-RC is a FILE STATUS and the two are deliberately not conflated - the '10' here is an end-of-file status, not a return code of ten. expectedMessages is empty because the subroutine contains no DISPLAY statement at all: 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' at CBSTM03A.CBL:359 belongs to the caller, and on '10' even the caller displays nothing - it sets END-OF-FILE and moves on. Two operation codes stay dark (practice B5). M03B-WRITE 'W' (:107) and M03B-REWRITE 'Z' (:108) are declared but are never SET anywhere in app/cbl, and neither appears as an operation in this case; they stay declared and unexercised rather than being invented into life. The unit (gate G12, requirement I3, practice B4). The prompt-mandated Java name is StatementGenerationJobB, but CBSTM03B is not a job: its own header at :7 reads 'BATCH COBOL Subroutine', no EXEC PGM=CBSTM03B appears in app/jcl, app/proc or app/csd, and CBSTM03A CALLs it thirteen times. It is therefore a Spring @Component and unitKind is COMPONENT; the name divergence is recorded here rather than quietly corrected. The component is driven directly, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). Provenance (practice B12). Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - from the line numbers cited here, from the CVACT03Y field offsets, and from the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt - and was NEVER captured from a COBOL execution. No COBOL runs in this environment: AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers, among them a COBOL compiler whose indexed file handler is disabled, which is precisely what an ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED file like this one would need. The deviation is one of provenance only - twenty cases per program, field-for-field diffing and a diff count of zero all stand - and it is escalated as risk R-A in AAP section 0.9.11.
